summary: Rate-limit oscillation observed during scheduled autoscaler eviction/rollout causing 429 spikes for low-latency chat traffic
description:
Issue summary:
BrightCart reports periodic waves of 429 responses for a subset of low-latency chat endpoints immediately after our scheduled autoscaler eviction window / rolling upgrade for their dedicated pool. 429 spikes last ~2-7 minutes and correlate with autoscaler node drain/eviction events and a flurry of short-lived client connections. This started after a recent autoscaler tuning change (reduce scale-down cooldown from 5m to 60s) and an internal canary rollout.

Impact:
- Customer (dedicated) experiencing degraded UX for real-time chat features; message send failures and retries.
- Estimated 12% of chat requests hit 429 during each eviction wave; top-level metrics show client-side retry storms.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool in prod-us-west (multi-tenant on a single pool for BrightCart)
- API traffic pattern: many short-lived connections, high request-per-connection, low token/payload size
- Autoscaler config was recently changed by Infrastructure team on 2026-03-08

Why this ticket created:
Customer asked for root cause and mitigation steps for production stability and requested guidance on rate-limit and autoscaler co-tuning for dedicated pools.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated pool with autoscaler cooldown 60s and start steady low-latency chat traffic from ~200 workers.
2) Trigger a scale-down or rolling node replacement (simulate eviction) causing active connections to be redistributed.
3) Observe API gateway and rate-limiter counters during eviction window (0-7 minutes).
4) Measure 429 rate on chat endpoints and correlate with per-route token accounting and ephemeral session counts.
logs: 2026-03-10T02:12:14Z gateway: 429 count spike +314 over 3m for route /v1/chat/stream (route-id chat-low-latency)
2026-03-10T02:12:16Z autoscaler: starting drain node i-0abc... reason=scheduled-rollout
2026-03-10T02:12:20Z serving-runtime: KV cache miss rate up 45% during connection migration
2026-03-10T02:15:40Z rate-limiter: per-tenant token-window refill drift detected relative to edge counter (delta=+9s)
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Rapid scale-down reduced total active serving capacity, increasing per-node request multiplexing and causing local token-window exhaustion on route-specific token buckets.
Hypothesis 2: Short-lived client connections (HTTP/2 and ephemeral API keys) cause duplicated accounting at edge and origin during reconnect, amplifying token consumption counts during eviction.
Metric snapshots show: tenant_total_capacity before=24 GPUs, during drain=18 GPUs, 429_rate baseline=0.2% => during drain=12.1%
Trace sampling (trace IDs provided to SRE) shows requests folded across different upstream hosts within the same second leading to token double-counts in edge aggregator.
Rate-limiter logs indicate 'window-sync-late' events coinciding with kube node cordon timestamps; edge refill epoch drifted by up to 11s in one instance.
We reproduced locally in a staging dedicated cluster by lowering scale-down cooldown and issuing 500 concurrent short-lived chat streams: observed similar 429 oscillation pattern.
comments: Support (Aisha): Collected customer logs and asked for time window and sample request IDs. Shared initial graph showing 3-minute 429 wave. Link: slack://support#SUP-980020
Customer (BrightCart - ops@brightcart.com): Provided SDK telemetry and confirmed they did a config change to client retry backoff yesterday. Mentioned they use ephemeral API keys per session.
SRE (Jordan Kim): Noted recent autoscaler tweak on 2026-03-08 to reduce cooldown. Scheduling to repro in staging with exact autoscaler settings.
Infra (Carlos Mendes): Pushed a canary PR that modified node cordon drain grace; referenced PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3221

Engineering (Serving runtime - Mei Wong): Observed that KV cache invalidation during host handoff increased per-request CPU spikes briefly which may reduce throughput and interact badly with rate windows.
action_items: Short-term workaround: advise BrightCart to add client-side retry jitter and increase backoff to avoid synchronized retry waves (recommend exponential backoff with jitter, initial backoff 200ms).
Apply server-side mitigation: temporarily increase per-route burst pool size for chat-low-latency route for this dedicated pool (config target: +30% burst capacity during drain windows).
Revert autoscaler cooldown to 5m on dedicated pools until refill epoch sync issues are resolved.
Patch rate-limiter: add 1s smoothing window to edge->origin refill handoff to avoid double-counting during host swap (PR linked).
Follow-up: run coordinated chaos test for node drain + short-lived connections to validate fixes.
resolution: Workaround and partial mitigation applied 2026-03-12: increased route burst pool for BrightCart's dedicated pool and reverted scale-down cooldown to 5m. PR to add 1s smoothing window merged to staging; scheduling rollout next week. Customer confirmed 429 spike amplitude reduced to <1% in two subsequent eviction windows. Recommended client-side jitter/backoff configuration provided in support reply.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12: Ops increased burst_pool_size by 30% for tenant brightcart-prod (manual config change).
2026-03-12: Infra reverted autoscaler cooldown to 300s for dedicated pools (rollback of 2026-03-08 tweak).
2026-03-13: Rate-limiter smoothing PR merged to main branch (will be staged deploy week of 2026-03-16).
Postmortem: follow-up ticket proposed to add coordinated integration test and improve observability for refill-epoch drift (INT-4412).
customer_communication: 2026-03-10: Initial acknowledgement sent within 1 hour; requested telemetry and sample request-ids.
2026-03-12: Notified customer of temporary burst pool increase and cooldown revert; customer accepted mitigation and ran smoke tests.
2026-03-13: Customer reported improved stability and agreed to staging validation for smoothing rollout.
